item.title: Persefoni
item.description:
Persefoni helps companies calculate and report their greenhouse gas emissions. It collects data from energy bills, travel, procurement, and suppliers, applies emission factors, and calculates totals for direct emissions, purchased energy, and value chain emissions. The system keeps an audit trail so figures can be verified.

Reporting is a main use. The platform produces disclosures aligned with frameworks such as the GHG Protocol, CDP, and regional regulations, and helps set and track reduction targets. An AI assistant answers questions about methodology and data, and supports tasks like mapping spend data to emission categories.

item.title: Pachama
item.description:
Pachama works on the trust problem in carbon markets. Credits from forest projects are only valuable if the forest is actually protected or restored, and checking this is hard. Pachama’s models analyze satellite and lidar data to estimate carbon stored in forests and to detect deforestation or degradation over time.

Buyers use its ratings and monitoring to choose credits and track them after purchase, and project developers use the data to support their claims. The company has also worked on tools for measuring forest carbon more cheaply than field surveys alone.

item.title: Patch
item.description:
Patch simplifies buying carbon removal. Companies browse projects, compare prices and methods, and purchase credits through a platform or API instead of negotiating deals one by one. Developers can embed purchases into other software, such as financial or e-commerce products.

The company has shifted toward helping enterprises plan and procure carbon removal at scale, with tools for sourcing, due diligence, and reporting. AI supports tasks like drafting requests for proposals and evaluating projects.

item.title: Sylvera
item.description:
Sylvera brings independent analysis to the carbon market. Analysts and models assess projects, such as forest protection or renewable energy, against criteria like additionality and permanence, and issue ratings. Satellite data and machine learning help measure forest carbon and detect deforestation.

Buyers use the ratings to choose credits, and sellers use them to demonstrate quality. The platform tracks market prices and supply, and supports due diligence.

Sylvera is sold on subscription to enterprises and financial institutions. Carbon markets remain contested, and ratings reflect methodology choices. Alternatives include BeZero Carbon, Pachama, MSCI Carbon Markets, Calyx Global, and Renoster. Sylvera suits buyers evaluating carbon credits.

item.title: Carbon Trust
item.description:
The Carbon Trust began as a UK organization set up to help businesses and the public sector cut emissions, and it now works internationally. It advises companies on how to measure their greenhouse gas emissions across operations and supply chains, set reduction targets, and plan the changes needed to meet them. Its work spans corporate carbon footprinting, product footprints, net zero strategy, and support with climate disclosure requirements.

A well-known part of its business is certification and standards. The Carbon Trust Standard recognizes organizations that measure and reduce their footprint, and other programs verify claims about products and supply chains. Software and data tools support these services, and AI is used to process large amounts of supplier and energy data, estimate emissions where measured data is missing, and identify the best reduction opportunities.

item.title: Climate TRACE
item.description: Climate TRACE exists because official emissions reporting is slow and incomplete. The coalition combines satellite images, sensor data, and public records and applies machine learning to estimate emissions from individual sources: power plants, steel mills, oil and gas fields, ships, aircraft, cement plants, farms, and more. The result is a global inventory that can be searched by country, sector, or even a single facility, updated more frequently than government reports.

item.title: Planet Labs
item.description: Planet Labs built its business on frequency. Rather than a few large satellites, it operates a large number of small ones, so it can photograph almost every part of the land surface regularly. That consistency allows users to watch change over time: crops growing, forests being cleared, ice melting, construction progressing, or ships moving. The imagery has a lower resolution than the sharpest commercial satellites but far greater frequency, and some higher-resolution satellites supplement it.

item.title: Watershed
item.description:
Watershed focuses on carbon accounting for large companies. Organizations connect data from finance systems, energy bills, travel, and suppliers, and the platform converts that activity data into greenhouse gas emissions across all scopes, including the harder-to-measure supply chain. The methods follow recognized standards and are designed to stand up to audits, which matters as more companies face disclosure rules.

Beyond measurement, the platform supports action. Companies set targets, model reduction scenarios, and track progress, and tools for engaging suppliers help gather better data and cut emissions in the value chain. Reporting features produce disclosures for frameworks and regulations, and AI helps classify purchases, fill gaps in data, and prepare reports, which reduces the manual effort that carbon accounting requires.
